questions.question: The Anglo-Mysore War ended with which of the following battles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Battle of Seringapatam**__.

__
 
• The **Anglo-Mysore War **ended with the battle of **Seringapatam.**
 
• The Anglo-Mysore Wars was a series of four military confrontations in India between **the British and the rulers of Mysore.**
 
• The British won a decisive victory at the **Battle** **of Seringapatam (1799)**.
 
 
• Tipu was killed during the defense of the city.

__
 
• The **third Anglo-Mysore War** came to an end with the **Treaty of Seringapatam in** **1792**.
 
• Tipu Sultan, the de-facto ruler of the** Kingdom of Mysore** ceded** half his kingdom** to the **British** which included the areas of** Malabar**, **Coorg**, **Baramahal**, and **Dindigul**.
 
• In this war, **Tipu Sultan** used **Mysorean rockets** which were the **first Ircon-Cased rocket** used by the** Mysorean army**.
 
• After the war, **Tipu Sultan territories** divided between **Hyderabad** and the **British**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chromosomal disorder?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Down's Syndrome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Down's Syndrome is a chromosomal disorder.

 
 
• Down's Syndrome is also known as trisomy 21.
 
• Down syndrome is a condition in which a child is born with an extra copy of their 21st chromosome.
 
• Down syndrome is a genetic condition that causes mild to serious physical and mental developmental delays and disabilities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Haemophilia**__

__
 
• Haemophilia is a hereditary **bleeding disorder** in which the blood does not clot properly.
 
• It is caused when blood does not have enough clotting factors.
 
• Haemophilia is known as **Christmas disease and royal disease.**
 
• The major types of this condition are **Hemophilia A (also known as classic hemophilia or factor VIII deficiency) and Hemophilia B (also known as Christmas disease or factor IX deficiency). **

**Sickle cell anaemia**__

__
 
• Sickle cell anemia is an** inherited red blood cell disorder** in which there aren't enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen throughout your body.
 
• Normally, RBCs are **shaped like discs**, which gives them the flexibility to travel through even the smallest blood vessels.
 
• In sickle cell anemia, the RBCs are **shaped like sickles or crescent moons.**
 
• This makes them **sticky and rigid and prone to getting trapped in small vessels**, which blocks blood from reaching different parts of the body. This can cause pain and tissue damage.

**Cystic fibrosis**__

 
• Cystic fibrosis is a **serious hereditary disease** that damages the **respiratory system and digestive systems.**
 
• The body produces thick and sticky mucus that can clog the lungs and obstruct the pancreas.
 
• Cystic fibrosis affects the cells that produce** sweat, mucus, and digestive enzymes.**
 
• Cystic fibrosis can be life-threatening, and people with the condition tend to have a **shorter-than-normal life span.**

**Bijapur**__

__**Akbar (AD 1556-1605)**__

Jahangir (AD 1605-1627)__

• He is known for the **promotion of art, culture, and architecture**, during his reign.
 
• **The Taj Mahal, Jama Masjid, and the Red Fort** are some of the magnificent structures built during his reign.
 
• He was **imprisoned** by his son Aurangzeb in Agra fort and died in captivity in AD 1658.
 
• Shahjahan was buried at **Taj Mahal (Agra)** besides his loving wife Mumtaz Mahal.

Aurangzeb (AD 1658-1707)__

 
• Aurangzeb was the third son of Shahjahan born in the city of **Dahod, Gujarat**.
 
• He defeated Dara at Dharmat (1658), Samugarh (1658), and Deorai in which Samugarh was the decisive one and Deorai was the last one.

• The **Coromandel Coast** is the southeastern coast region of the Indian subcontinent, bounded by the Utkal Plains to the north, the Bay of Bengal to the east, the Kaveri delta to the south, and the Eastern Ghats to the west.
 
• The Coromandal coast extends over an area of about **22,800** square kilometers.

• The alluvial plains created by these rivers are **fertile and favour agriculture**.

• The Coromandel Coast falls in the **rain shadow of the Western Ghats** and receives a good deal less rainfall during the **summer southwest monsoon**, which contributes heavily to rainfall in the rest of India.

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with the enactment of the First Factories Act, 1881, which had provisions for regulating child employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon**__.

__
 
• **Lord Ripon** is credited with the enactment of the First Factories Act, 1881, which had provisions for regulating child employment.
 
• The **act** prohibited the working of **children** below seven years and a limited number of working hours for **children** below 12 years. 
 
• This **Act** also made **provision** of one hour break during the working period and four monthly holidays for the **employment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__**Lord Ripon**__

__
 
• The viceroy is known as **'The popular viceroy'.**
 
• In 1881, the **First official Census** in India was done by **Ripon.**
 
• **Hunter Commission **was appointed by **Ripon in 1882.**
 
• He was famously known as the **'Father of Local Self Government Act'** in 1882.
 
• **Repealed the Vernacular Press Act** in 1882
 
• **Hunter Commission** was appointed by Ripon in 1882 for **Educational reforms.**
 
• The viceroy during the time of **Ilbert Bill Controversy in 1883.**
 
• The viceroy raised the **age limit of Civil Service from 19 to 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Lord Irwin**__

__
 
• The viceroy is popularly known as the** 'Christian viceroy'.**
 
• The viceroy during the arrival of** Simon Commission in 1928 and Butler Commission in 1927.**
 
• **Poorna Swaraj Resolution and The Deepavali Declaration** were passed by Irwin in 1929. 
 
• Lord Irwin was the viceroy when the **First Round Table Conference** in England in1930.
 
• The viceroy during the **Dandi March **on **12th March 1930.**
 
• In **1931, Gandhi-Irwin ****Pact** was signed between Gandhiji and Irwin.
 
• **Sard Act (1929)**, which prohibits the marriage of girls below 14 and boys below 18 years of age was passed by Lord Irwin.

**Lord Mayo**__

__
 
• The viceroy introduces **financial decentralization** in India and made the **first Provincial Settlement** in 1870.
 
• He established the **Department of Agriculture and Commerce.**
 
• The **Indian Evidence Act** was passed by Lord Mayo in 1872.
 
• The **first census **was conducted by Lord Mayo in **1872.**
 
• The viceroy **murdered in office** by a convict **(Sher Ali) in Andaman in 1872.**

**Lord Curzon**__

 
• The British viceroy appointed the **'University Education Commission' in 1902.**
 
• **Indian Universities Act **passed in 1904.
 
• The **Partition of Bengal **on** 16th October 1905**
 
• **Indian Coinage and Paper Currency Act** passed in 1899.
 
• The** Archaeological Survey of India** was organized by Lord Curzon.
 
• A new **Department of Commerce and Industry** established.
